front: Kc for aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD
back: Kc = [C]^c[D]^d / ([A]^a[B]^b), with equilibrium concentrations in mol dm⁻³.
p(A) = mole fraction of A × total pressure; mole fraction = n(A)/n(total).

front: Kp for aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD (gases)
back: Kp = p(C)^c p(D)^d / (p(A)^a p(B)^b), using equilibrium partial pressures.
Substitute mol dm⁻³ for each term and cancel; e.g. N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ gives dm⁶ mol⁻²; equal powers give no units.
K ≫ 1: equilibrium lies to the right (mostly products); K ≪ 1: lies to the left.
Only temperature. Exothermic forward reaction: K falls as T rises; endothermic: K rises.
Reversed: K becomes 1/K. All coefficients doubled: K is squared; halved: square root.
Initial amounts → change (from the mole ratio) → equilibrium amounts → concentrations (÷ V) or partial pressures → K.
Only gases; solids and pure liquids are left out.
